newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Gerdau plans div, capital hikes for 3 firms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Gerdau plans div, capital hikes for 3 firms.

text.p: Officials at Brazil's Gerdau steel group plan to ask shareholders Oct 23 to cancel founders shares of three companies, a move likely to boost stock dividends paid out by those companies by 11 percent.
"The increase in dividends will be a consequence of the cancellation of those shares," Jose Peters, Gerdau's director of market relations, told Reuters.

Group officials also said they will propose a total 160 million reais in capital increases for Metalurgica Gerdau S.A., Siderurgica Riograndense S.A. and Cia Siderurgica da Guanabara (Cosigua) through a share subscription.
A proposals are part of a group restructuring begun in 1995, group administrators said in a statement.
Under Brazilian law, founder shares issued at the time the companies were formed have no expiration date and give the holder a right to 10 percent of annual net profit.

The shares have enabled Gerdau to reinvest sizeable portions of the company earnings. In 1995, Gerdau's gross sales rose to $2.2 billion, and this year it is expected to produce an estimated 3.4 million metric tons of steel.
The elimination of the founder shares would enable the group's firms to take advantage of improved market position and new capital market conditions, the statement said.
Moreover, "elimination of the founder shares will foster, from the second half of 1996, a greater flow of dividends to shareholders," it said.
A consultant's study shows Metalurgica Gerdau founder shares are valued 16.4 million reais, Siderurgica Riograndense's 31.1 million reais and Cosigua 43.1 million reais, the statement said.

Meanwhile, stockholders would be allowed to subscribe, from Oct 28 to Nov 26, for 260.3 shares of Metalurgica, 449.55 shares of Riograndense and 603.98 shares of Cosigua per 1,000 shares owned in each company, it said.
Capital raised would be reinvested: 29 million reais for Metalurgica, 55 million reais for Riograndense and 76 million reais for Cosigua, it added.
Administrators also said they will propose at a Nov 29 shareholders meeting the merger of Siderurgica Aconorte S.A. into Cosigua, foring a new firm named Gerdau S.A. Siderurgia.
"After this merger, all Grupo Gerdau's steel activities in Brazil will be conducted by (four) companies, with improved synergism among the units they will operate," it added.
